question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund IFSC is a Category III AIF registered in GIFT-IFSC with business income of INR 50 crore in FY 2025-26. Under Section 80LA, the fund claims the optional 100% tax holiday for 10 consecutive years out of the first 15. Ignoring surcharge/cess, the federal income-tax liability on business income in the holiday year is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 80LA permits a 100% deduction of income from specified IFSC activities for any 10 consecutive assessment years out of the first 15 beginning with the year of registration. In the holiday year, income-tax on the Rs 50 cr is NIL. This is a primary reason many Cat III funds domicile in GIFT-IFSC. The Trap: A applies the normal Cat III MMR. B uses the corporate rate without 80LA. D picks the concessional corporate rate, still ignoring 80LA. All three miss the IFSC tax-holiday punch. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-E both emphasise IFSC 80LA as a Cat III relocation lever. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) mentions IFSC only briefly. XIX-D (Cat I/II) rarely uses IFSC 80LA since Cat I/II enjoys pass-through onshore. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pitch 80LA to anchor LPs as a 40-point tax saving versus onshore Cat III — but remember the holiday is on INCOME-tax, not GST on management fees (GST from non-resident LPs is itself zero-rated in IFSC). Model the 10-of-15 election carefully: time the window to start when AUM (and hence fee/PnL) is ramping.
